title: Stephen said quietly.
html_source:
Stephen is feminized by Joyce or made less male/hero like – a deliberate act in gender criticism terms. In racial analysis, the intent of Joyce is less clear: the British attempted to render the Irish negroes, simian and unhuman but also late in the 1800s, the establishment in Britain described them in less dominant male terms and in more submissive female terms (Vincent J. Cheng). Did Joyce intend to raise the issue of racial profiling of the Irish by the British establishment or was he inventing the new man?

He also says this “quietly” probably because he doesn’t want to risk having his question about Haines overheard. He’s also pretty tired.
